contract.words: Collect $2,500 of settled cash within 28 days with no more than 3 hours a week of owner time.

terms.proofCondition: Settled cash of at least the target received within the window

strategy.title: No plan inside 3 owner hours a week: the agreed appraisals need 40 owner hours
strategy.why: Eight shops signed engagement letters at $350 ($2,800 >= $2,500), settling in 7 days, but the record names the owner personally as the appraiser at 5 hours per appraisal. Reaching $2,500 needs 8 appraisals = 40 owner hours, against 12 allowed (3 h/week x 4 weeks); 12 hours fund only 2 appraisals ($700).

alternatives.title: Do the 2 appraisals that fit in 12 hours
Subcontract the appraisals
alternatives.why: No other appraiser is named on the record; a fulfiller must exist.

noPlan.decisiveGap: Owner time: the only fulfiller is the owner, and the 8 appraisals the target needs take 40 owner hours against the 12 the objective allows.
noPlan.resolution: Allow at least 40 owner hours over the 28 days (10 h/week), or name a qualified appraiser who can perform the work so the owner's hours fall within 3 per week, then re-plan.

constraints.suggestion: Allow at least 40 owner hours over the 28 days (about 10 hours a week)

Eight shops signed engagement letters at $350 per appraisal.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN with an OWNER_HOURS constraint is correct. Eight written acceptances at $350 ($2,800 >= $2,500) settle in 7 days, so demand, price, conversion and settlement are established. But the card's fulfillmentOwner is 'The owner, personally' with humanHours 5 per appraisal, and the contract allows 3 owner hours a week. $2,500 / $350 = 7.14 -> 8 appraisals = 40 owner hours, against 3 x 4 = 12 hours in 28 days, which funds only 2 appraisals (10 h) = $700. The disagreement with Brain's FULFILMENT 'ok' is justified from the card's own humanHours and fulfillmentOwner fields, and Brain's own check reaches the same 40-vs-12 conclusion. Subcontracting is rightly not assumed: no other fulfiller is recorded.
findings: Arithmetic verified: 8 x 5 h = 40 h; 12 h allowed; floor(12/5) = 2 appraisals = $700 = 28% of target.
Even 7 appraisals ($2,450) would fall short, so 8 is the true minimum and 35 h would not suffice either.
Fulfilment rests on a PERSON fact (the owner says they do it); the plan correctly treats the owner as the only recorded performer rather than inventing one.
Resolution names both levers (raise hours to ~10/week, or a named qualified appraiser), which is what the evidence decides.
